margin_sensitivity.note: regret of each policy when the truth is -1.5 and the point estimate is -2.2, as gross margin varies; the method is inert where the DP declines to mark down at all

refused_margins.reason: ladder floor is at or below unit cost; nothing to discount into
ladder floor is at or below unit cost; nothing to discount into

scale_invariance.note: regret in pp across a 8x range of season size; small spread supports the rescaling

real.source: UCI Online Retail II via data/runs/real_run.json

decision_degenerate.why: on a wholly inelastic interval, cutting price loses on margin and does not make it back on volume, so full price is optimal at every elasticity in the set; all four policies emit the same ladder and every regret is identically zero. This is the correct behaviour of the DP, not a limitation of the robust operator — there is simply no decision for robustness to protect.

real.caveat: No true elasticity exists on real data. These are regrets across each SKU's own DML confidence interval, not realised profit. They also cover only the decision-relevant subset; see decision_degenerate for the rest.
inherited_assumptions: unit_cost derived from an assumed 45% gross margin; no public retail dataset carries COGS
elasticity fitted on list_price, not realised price, because realised price moves with order-size mix under this retailer's volume discounts

scenario_assumptions.note: UCI has no season, opening buy, or salvage; these are ours.

floor_calibration.note: certificate covers parameter error, not demand noise; the season-level violation rate is reported so the distinction is not left to be assumed

joint.caveat: domain randomisation optimises the mean over the interval, not its tail; no certificate is available here, unlike the single-SKU operator
